purpose: receive a real Safaricom callback on the secret path and prove a real 1037 does not fail the payment
method: payments run locally with MPESA_MODE=daraja behind an ngrok HTTPS tunnel used as CallBackURL, charging through POST /internal/v1/charges against a stub POS. Sandbox credentials only, nothing deployed, no AWS change.
findings: Safaricom does post callbacks, from 196.201.212.69, 26s after the push. An earlier probe of ours saw none in 372s; that probe's conclusion was wrong and its file is removed.
The secret path segment authenticates a real Daraja callback. The HMAC route could not have: Safaricom sends no signature, so every real callback would have been 401.

A real 1037 callback did not fail the payment. It stayed pending with no failure_reason and no timed_out_at, exactly as ADR-002 requires. The provider saying 'no response from user' is not the provider saying 'declined'.
The callback is logged either way. A wrong secret is refused 401 and recorded as rejected_bad_signature with reason path_secret_mismatch.
limits: One push, one shortcode, one unanswered payer, in the sandbox. The deployed service still runs MPESA_MODE=fake; enabling this path in production needs task-definition environment variables that live in the platform area.
